Draft proposal only. No ML consumer is a prerequisite. All procedures and proofs remain to be authored.

### P-NUM-ODE-01 — One-step ODE consistency and local error

**Pages:** one-step-ode-consistency-and-local-error / one-step-ode-consistency-and-local-error-examples. **Scope:** Define a one-step method $\Psi_h(t,y)$, local defect $\|\Psi_h(t,y(t))-y(t+h)\|$, and stability. For a fixed interval $[0,T]$ and exact solutions staying in a compact tube, state the order-$p$ hypothesis as a uniform local defect $\le Ch^{p+1}$ and the one-step stability bound $\|\Psi_h(t,u)-\Psi_h(t,v)\|\le(1+Lh)\|u-v\|$. Derive these premises for Euler when $f$ is $C^1$ in time and state with bounded derivatives on that tube; any named Runge–Kutta method must state its order conditions and required derivatives separately. **Proof route:** Taylor-expand the exact flow and the selected method increment, bound remainders uniformly on the tube, and prove the stated stability estimate; do not infer an order from the method label alone. **Examples:** Euler on a scalar linear field; a nonsmooth field where its local order drops. **Requires:** thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-a-maximal-ode-solution, thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives, and a proved Taylor remainder estimate; the local error calculation is explicit, but a numerical-analysis source remains unaudited. **Sources:** Chen et al., neural-ODE Appendix B/C and numerical issues, PDF pp. 13–16, and Papamakarios et al., continuous-flow section pp. 31–33, discuss solver use but do not prove the error theorem. Acquire/read a matching numerical-ODE source before publication. This pair precedes P-NUM-ODE-02.

### P-NUM-ODE-02 — Global ODE and log-density integration error

**Pages:** global-ode-and-density-error / global-ode-and-density-error-examples. **Scope:** Under P-NUM-ODE-01’s uniform order-$p$ defect/stability bounds and a fixed finite interval, derive $\max_n\|y_n-y(t_n)\|\le C_T h^p$ by the discrete Grönwall recurrence. For a continuous normalizing flow augment the state by $\ell'=-\operatorname{div}f(x,t)$ and bound the log-density error separately. For Euler, $f\in C^2$ with bounded derivatives on a compact tube makes the augmented vector field locally Lipschitz and supports a local $O(h^2)$ defect; for order $p>1$, require the method-specific order conditions and enough bounded derivatives of the augmented field, or state a separate quadrature theorem with matching smoothness. $C^2$ regularity alone does not justify arbitrary order-$p$ convergence. State solver, quadrature, and state-error contributions separately. A state trajectory error alone does not control log-density or adjoint-gradient error. **Proof route:** derive $e_{n+1}\le(1+Lh)e_n+Ch^{p+1}$, iterate it, then apply a second bound to the augmented/log-density component under its own local defect and stability estimates. **Examples:** Euler global error for a linear flow; same state solver with a separately refined density quadrature. **Requires:** P-NUM-ODE-01 — One-step ODE consistency and local error; discrete Grönwall and the divergence-Lipschitz estimate, proved locally if no exact supplier exists. **Sources:** Chen et al. pp. 13–16 and Papamakarios et al. pp. 31–33 discuss solver use and numerical issues but do not prove these error theorems; the local defect/stability/Grönwall proof remains a clearly specified authoring obligation. ML-58 — Neural ODEs and continuous normalizing flows and ML-61 — Conditional flow matching and transport paths consume this only when numerical error is claimed.


## Binding consumed contract

**P-NUM-ODE-01/02.** Fix d≥1, T>0, h=T/N, N≥1, a common open time-state domain and a compact solution tube with positive margin. Use Euclidean vector norms and induced operator norms. The exact IVP solution y and every numerical stage/state in the theorem stay in that tube. A one-step map Ψ_h(t,·) is defined there and satisfies, for constants C,L≥0 independent of N and j, ||Ψ_h(t_j,y(t_j))−y(t_(j+1))||≤C h^(p+1) and ||Ψ_h(t_j,v)−Ψ_h(t_j,w)||≤(1+Lh)||v−w||. Derive Euler's C and L from f∈C¹ with finite field, time-derivative and state-Jacobian bounds on the tube; derive each higher-order tableau's defect separately from its exact derivative/order conditions. For augmented log density ℓ′=−div f, Euler requires f∈C² with bounded relevant derivatives of f and div f, the augmented tube, and a separate state/log-defect estimate; no arbitrary higher order follows from C². Local proof route: Taylor/integral remainder, invariant-tube admissibility and geometric-sum recurrence, using actual root ODE/Taylor/Grönwall suppliers. Matching source design: Hairer–Wanner Ch. III §§III.2–III.5, PDF pp. 4–11/printed 60–67, as recorded by the recovery packet. NA-15 supplies concrete conditions to instantiate the abstract theorem, never a prerequisite of the generic theorem. Consumers: NA-15, NA-18 notation only, NA-21 when numerical shooting is quantified, NA-45 matching ODE terms.

Multidimensional commutative noise extension after proving L_i sigma_j=L_j sigma_i yields symmetrized iterated integrals; noncommuting noise requires Levy areas with their own sampling approximation error and cost. Also supply scalar additive-noise stochastic Heun: Z=Y+b(Y)h+sigma DeltaW, Ynew=Y+0.5h[b(Y)+b(Z)]+sigma DeltaW, constant sigma. Prove weak order2 for b in C_b^6 and payoff backward solution with the actual mixed derivatives through spatial order6/time order3 bounded, by one-step moment matching through h² and O(h³) remainder. This specific weak2 guarantee does not extend to multiplicative noise without extra terms. New Milstein MLMC delta: nested commutative-Milstein paths have E|Yfine-Ycoarse|²=O(h²), hence Lipschitz payoff variance O(h²); with cost O(h^-1) and bias O(h) consume canonical MLMC theorem to obtain O(eps^-2). **Proof/prereqs:** same-pair iterated Itô integral identity I_11=((DeltaW)^2-h)/2, conditional moments/orthogonality, local mean O(h²), local RMS O(h^(3/2)) and stochastic stability recurrence proving global order1. General stochastic local-to-global theorem is authored here; existing deterministic theorem insufficient. **B:** geometric Brownian motion, scalar multiplicative noise, noncommuting two-noise area term. **Cost:** derivatives and Gaussian/area samples; arbitrary Levy areas not free. **Sources:** Kloeden/Platen, Numerical Solution of SDEs, Itô-Taylor and strong approximation chapters; Higham, SIAM Review 43 (2001), Milstein section. **Disposition:** extend-existing substantial algorithm/error guarantee. `ex-quantile-coupling-on-the-real-line` already proves generalized inverse Q(U) has the target law; `lem-randomized-probability-integral-transform` treats the reverse randomized CDF transform. Do not redefine those statistical transformations as a new method. The example is contextual rather than a legal logical supplier; consume `thm-probability-law-and-distribution-function-correspondence` and promote only the needed generalized-inverse sublevel identity to a typed prerequisite with proof/source attribution, avoiding a duplicate broad quantile-coupling theorem. The new guarantee is actual bit/stream implementation and finite-distribution error plus Box-Muller sampling, absent from inspected canonical methods.

**Randomness model:** independent ideal fair bits B_j on an explicitly constructed countable product probability space; U=sum B_j 2^-j has uniform law by dyadic cylinder intervals and continuity of measure. Disjoint bit blocks/streams preserve independence. A b-bit K uniform on {0,...,2^b-1} gives U_b=(K+1/2)2^-b, coupling |U-U_b|<=2^(-b-1), hence W1 at most that and Kolmogorov discrepancy at most 2^-b. Finite-support versus continuous law has total variation distance1, so no TV-small assertion. Independence of finite outputs requires disjoint independent bit blocks; recycling bits changes dependence.

**Practical finite generators:** define an actual full-period LCG modulo 2^w with odd increment and multiplier a congruent1 mod4, w>=2; prove full period by induction modulo powers of2 using affine iterate arithmetic, and state finite state/period bound for every deterministic generator. With random uniform initial state each single state is uniform, but adjacent states satisfy the recurrence and are not independent. Give a counter-based stream interface as a deterministic keyed permutation of finite counters; a random permutation/key model or computational pseudorandomness assumption must be explicit, never an IID theorem. No cryptographic-quality claim or empirical-test proof of independence. Non-overlapping blocks avoid exact reuse only within certified period; do not imply probabilistic independence.

**Variates:** inverse CDF already canonical; add implemented bracketed inverse with certified |F(xhat)-u|<=epsilon on a monotone continuous CDF, finite-bit U discrepancy adds to Kolmogorov error (plus any actual CDF approximation error). Spatial error requires density f>=m>0 on the inversion bracket, and tails handled separately. Discrete CDF binary search gives exact categorical law under ideal U, finite-bit count discrepancy bounded per threshold; Bernoulli rational sampling via unbiased integer rejection has geometric expected bit/block cost and budget failure; finite budget discarded separately.

Box-Muller uses independent ideal U1,U2 in (0,1), Z1=sqrt(-2 log U1)cos(2pi U2), Z2=sqrt(-2 log U1)sin(2pi U2). Prove independent standard-normal density by polar change of variables and product density normalization; same-pair polar Jacobian/measure change prerequisite must be proved if not published. Finite bits imply bounded normal tails and discrete output, never exact Gaussian; couple midpoint U_b to U, restrict U1>=delta and guard angular/endpoint arithmetic, derivative bounds give explicit Wasserstein/bounded-Lipschitz output error on that event, while discarded event probability <=delta+2^-b. Tail expectations use proved Gaussian/Rayleigh moments and Cauchy-Schwarz; elementary log/sqrt/trig evaluation errors supplied by precision owner add through those derivative bounds. No Ziggurat implementation required if not fully specified/proved; rejection algorithm may be a later optional genuinely new optimization only with envelope/area proof. Gaussian samples in SDE algorithms are ideal-law or approximate-law with this additional coupling error propagated; no invisible exact-normal finite-bit oracle.

**Same-frontier prerequisites:** product independent-bit construction (reuse existing countable product theorem if available, otherwise own cylinder extension), dyadic uniform law, LCG modular induction, stopping/rejection cost, finite-CDF inverse residual, polar transform identity, truncated-transform coupling and arithmetic error propagation. Root must map any newly located canonical supplier instead of creating duplicate items. **Examples:** low-bit LCG correlation/lattice, normal tail truncation, zero endpoint log failure, inverse CDF near vanishing density. **Cost:** random bits, rejection count, integer arithmetic, precision and transform calls; bit cost distinct from real-RAM sampling oracle cost. **Sources, unread candidates:** Devroye, Non-Uniform Random Variate Generation, author's full-book portal https://luc.devroye.org/rnbookindex.html ; L'Ecuyer RNG publications https://www.iro.umontreal.ca/~lecuyer/myftp/papers.html ; Box/Muller, Ann Math Stat 29 (1958), https://doi.org/10.1214/aoms/1177706645 . Canonical quantile source https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf .

# Independent numerical ODE prerequisite pairs — intake proposal

Draft proposal only. No ML consumer is a prerequisite. All procedures and proofs remain to be authored.

### P-NUM-ODE-01 — One-step ODE consistency and local error

**Pages:** one-step-ode-consistency-and-local-error / one-step-ode-consistency-and-local-error-examples. **Scope:** Define a one-step method $\Psi_h(t,y)$, local defect $\|\Psi_h(t,y(t))-y(t+h)\|$, and stability. For a fixed interval $[0,T]$ and exact solutions staying in a compact tube, state the order-$p$ hypothesis as a uniform local defect $\le Ch^{p+1}$ and the one-step stability bound $\|\Psi_h(t,u)-\Psi_h(t,v)\|\le(1+Lh)\|u-v\|$. Derive these premises for Euler when $f$ is $C^1$ in time and state with bounded derivatives on that tube; any named Runge–Kutta method must state its order conditions and required derivatives separately. **Proof route:** Taylor-expand the exact flow and the selected method increment, bound remainders uniformly on the tube, and prove the stated stability estimate; do not infer an order from the method label alone. **Examples:** Euler on a scalar linear field; a nonsmooth field where its local order drops. **Requires:** thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-a-maximal-ode-solution, thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives, and a proved Taylor remainder estimate; the local error calculation is explicit, but a numerical-analysis source remains unaudited. **Sources:** Chen et al., neural-ODE Appendix B/C and numerical issues, PDF pp. 13–16, and Papamakarios et al., continuous-flow section pp. 31–33, discuss solver use but do not prove the error theorem. Acquire/read a matching numerical-ODE source before publication. This pair precedes P-NUM-ODE-02.

### P-NUM-ODE-02 — Global ODE and log-density integration error

**Pages:** global-ode-and-density-error / global-ode-and-density-error-examples. **Scope:** Under P-NUM-ODE-01’s uniform order-$p$ defect/stability bounds and a fixed finite interval, derive $\max_n\|y_n-y(t_n)\|\le C_T h^p$ by the discrete Grönwall recurrence. For a continuous normalizing flow augment the state by $\ell'=-\operatorname{div}f(x,t)$ and bound the log-density error separately. For Euler, $f\in C^2$ with bounded derivatives on a compact tube makes the augmented vector field locally Lipschitz and supports a local $O(h^2)$ defect; for order $p>1$, require the method-specific order conditions and enough bounded derivatives of the augmented field, or state a separate quadrature theorem with matching smoothness. $C^2$ regularity alone does not justify arbitrary order-$p$ convergence. State solver, quadrature, and state-error contributions separately. A state trajectory error alone does not control log-density or adjoint-gradient error. **Proof route:** derive $e_{n+1}\le(1+Lh)e_n+Ch^{p+1}$, iterate it, then apply a second bound to the augmented/log-density component under its own local defect and stability estimates. **Examples:** Euler global error for a linear flow; same state solver with a separately refined density quadrature. **Requires:** P-NUM-ODE-01 — One-step ODE consistency and local error; discrete Grönwall and the divergence-Lipschitz estimate, proved locally if no exact supplier exists. **Sources:** Chen et al. pp. 13–16 and Papamakarios et al. pp. 31–33 discuss solver use and numerical issues but do not prove these error theorems; the local defect/stability/Grönwall proof remains a clearly specified authoring obligation. ML-58 — Neural ODEs and continuous normalizing flows and ML-61 — Conditional flow matching and transport paths consume this only when numerical error is claimed.

If the forward Euler map preserves a specified convex invariant set C or satisfies a convex functional Phi(u+h f(u))<=Phi(u) for every u in C and 0<=h<=h_FE, convexity of C/Phi proves every stage and update preserve that property with coefficient1 and same timestep bound. **Stabilized explicit method:** first order R_s(z)=T_s(1+z/s²), s>=1, implemented by y0=y, y1=y+(h/s²)Ay and yj=2 y_(j-1)-y_(j-2)+(2h/s²)A y_(j-1). For the second-order linear RKC variant s>=2, use w1=3/(s²-1), b=(s²-1)/(3s²), a=1-b and R_s(z)=a+b T_s(1+w1 z). Evaluate the same three-term Chebyshev recurrence with h/s² replaced by w1 h and output a y0+b ys. Preserve the simple linear proof above as the stability model, and include this actual autonomous nonlinear second-order stabilized explicit RK recurrence. For s>=2 set w1=3/(s²-1), b0=b1=b2=1/4 and b_j=(j²-1)/(3j²) for j>=2, a_j=1-b_j. Let Y0=y, Y1=y+b1 w1 h f(y). For j=2,...,s define mu_j=2 b_j/b_(j-1), nu_j=-b_j/b_(j-2), mt_j=2 b_j w1/b_(j-1), gt_j=-a_(j-1) mt_j, and

Yj=(1-mu_j-nu_j)y+mu_j Y_(j-1)+nu_j Y_(j-2)+mt_j h f(Y_(j-1))+gt_j h f(y).

At constant f its stage abscissae follow c1=b1 w1 and c_j=b_j w1 j² for j>=2, hence c_s=1. **Disposition:** genuinely-new. No canonical Parareal/MGRIT carrier located by filename/content searches. **Methods:** for fine propagator F and coarse G over macro H, U0^k=u0, U_(n+1)^(k+1)=G(U_n^(k+1))+F(U_n^k)-G(U_n^k); initialize by serial G. Parallel F evaluations followed by serial coarse correction; finite sweep/time budgets. Target is the sequential fine trajectory, not the exact ODE unless F's error is added.

**Proof:** consistency induction proves U_n^k=F^n(u0) for n<=k, hence exact fine solution after at most N sweeps in exact arithmetic, independent of a contraction assertion. For useful convergence, assume on a common invariant tube ||G(x)-G(y)||<=a||x-y|| and ||(F-G)(x)-(F-G)(y)||<=b||x-y||, with a<=1+CH, b<=C H^(q+1). Error recurrence e_(n+1)^(k+1)<=a e_n^(k+1)+b e_n^k yields by induction binomial(n,k)b^k max(1,a)^n times a bounded initial-error envelope, with endpoint conventions and all iterates remaining in tube; fixed T then gives iteration-dependent acceleration. Prove exact coarse elimination identity by block substitution. Scalar commuting diffusion example yields an explicit matrix and its bound; no mesh-independent convergence from the algorithm's name. Multilevel recursive cycle requires separately bounded level operators and recursion, not transfer of two-grid contraction.

## XD-03 — conservative positive production–destruction integrators

**Pages:** `positive-conservative-production-destruction-integrators` / companion. **New method:** modified Patankar families, with no claim that A-stability, symplecticity or generic RK order implies positivity.

**Exact scope.** Nonnegative finite compartments y_i with pair transfers p_ij(y)=d_ji(y)≥0 and `y_i′=Σ_j(p_ij−d_ij)` (external sources/sinks separately specified). First-order Patankar Euler uses transfers frozen at y^n with destination/source weights `y_j^{n+1}/σ_j`, where σ_j>0 is declared and, for first-order consistency, σ_j=y_j^n under a uniform positive lower bound. The resulting matrix has nonpositive off-diagonals, positive diagonal and strict column dominance; prove inverse nonnegativity, positivity and exact summed conservation. Handle initially zero compartments by an explicit zero-consistent transfer-factor representation or a separately analyzed positive denominator regularization; `0/0=0` cannot silently preserve the order proof. The specified second-order positive-interior scheme is MPRK22(1): compute the stage z by Patankar Euler with denominator y^n; then solve `y_i^{n+1}=y_i^n+Δt Σ_j[(p_ij(y^n)+p_ij(z)) y_j^{n+1}/(2z_j)−(d_ij(y^n)+d_ij(z)) y_i^{n+1}/(2z_i)]`. Prove second order on a compact smooth positive tube with uniformly positive stage denominators; conservation/positivity hold independently of that Taylor estimate. Zero-stage and denominator-regularized variants have separate declared contracts, rather than borrowing this order theorem. Do not assert all Patankar variants are second order.

**Proof route / local ownership.** Own finite M-matrix inverse positivity by a nonnegative Neumann series after diagonal scaling, strict dominance/invertibility, conservative column-sum identity, admissible zero-state transfer representation, uniform coefficient bounds, local defect and global order on a compact positive tube. These are not supplied by scalar stiff stability. Derive a residual-to-mass/positivity ledger for inexact solves; positivity after rounded solves is conditional on certified component bounds or a separately analyzed conservative correction. A tiny linear residual alone is not positivity.

**B examples.** Two-compartment stiff reversible transfer; three-species stoichiometric conservation, with explicit conversion from number to weighted mass variables; extinction/zero-component corner showing denominator failure; explicit Euler negative concentration despite correct first-order truncation. Stipulate kinetics; no empirical reaction law becomes a theorem.

**Dependencies.** NA-01/02/15/17, independent ODE; XD-01 generator positivity as reusable special case. **Sources:** Burchard–Deleersnijder–Meister, “A high-order conservative Patankar-type discretisation for stiff systems of production–destruction equations,” Applied Numerical Mathematics 47 (2003), pp. 1–30, DOI `10.1016/S0168-9274(03)00101-6`; Kopecz–Meister, “On order conditions for modified Patankar–Runge–Kutta schemes,” Applied Numerical Mathematics 123 (2018), pp. 159–179, DOI `10.1016/j.apnum.2017.09.004`. Read actual stage formulas/order conditions before committing a particular second-order carrier.

source_record_verbatim.promise_and_proof_design_verbatim:
**Disposition:** extend-existing numerical guarantee; consume NA15 RK/collocation and NA21 BVP collocation where actually established; this pair concerns IVP high-order quadrature and iterative solution, not duplicate BVP definitions.

On [t,t+h] with distinct nodes c_i in [0,1], let Q_ij=integral_0^ci l_j(s)ds from Lagrange basis. Collocation stage vector satisfies U=1 tensor u+h Q F(U). Explicitly define lower-triangular Q_delta from node-subinterval Euler quadrature; SDC sweep solves U^(k+1)=1 tensor u+h Q_delta F(U^(k+1))+h(Q-Q_delta)F(U^k), component by component with selected implicit branches or explicit preconditioner. If h L||Q_delta||<1, inverse Lipschitz inequality gives contraction factor q=h L||Q-Q_delta||/(1-h L||Q_delta||)<1. Prove stage fixed point equals collocation, geometric iteration residual bound, and finite budget reports nonconvergence. With sufficiently small h and constant predictor, each sweep reduces stage error by O(h); derive the actual order-vs-sweep index rather than promise unlimited order.

Prove local defect O(h^(M+1)) for M nodes from interpolation remainder assuming C^M smooth integrand along the exact flow, and stable propagation gives at least global order M for a step endpoint derived from the same quadrature. Gauss nodes endpoint superconvergence order2M is a separate full proof obligation using orthogonality/defect adjoint or exact RK order conditions; it cannot be inferred from polynomial degree alone. Include one fully proved Gauss-midpoint order2 case even before general superconvergence. Chosen iteration tolerance ||U-U*||<=C h^(p+1) yields collocation order p after accounting for endpoint h F sensitivity; a residual-to-stage inverse bound must convert stopping residual. Spectral node interpolation may have large Lebesgue constants; expose M dependence. No claim of stiff convergence when h L is large; preconditioned scalar linear iteration matrix (I-h lambda Q_delta)^-1 h lambda(Q-Q_delta) is computed and its norm/radius/powers analyzed separately.

**Prerequisites owned here:** node quadrature matrix identity, inverse residual bound, contraction and finite-sweep error, collocation interpolation residual, optional Gauss superconvergence proof. **Examples:** nonstiff high-order IVP, stiff SDC iteration divergence, too-few sweeps dropping order, inexact linear solves. **Cost:** M RHS/stage solves per sweep, reuse of old stage RHS explicitly counted, collocation matrix setup and precision. **Sources, unread candidates:** Dutt/Greengard/Rokhlin, BIT 40 (2000), spectral deferred corrections, https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1022338906936 ; Hairer collocation/RK source https://www.unige.ch/~hairer/poly/chap3.pdf . Exact sections must be read before source acceptance.

source_record_verbatim.cycle2_collision_addendum:
### T10/T11 hard-sphere addendum

For finitely many spherical particles with masses m_i>0, radii r_i>0 and smooth external forces on a compact separated configuration tube, define pair guard ||q_i-q_j||-(r_i+r_j). An isolated binary impact has unit normal n=(q_i-q_j)/||q_i-q_j|| and preimpact relative normal velocity v_n=(v_i-v_j) dot n<0. For prescribed restitution e in [0,1], impulse J=-(1+e)v_n/(1/m_i+1/m_j) gives v_i^+=v_i^-+J n/m_i, v_j^+=v_j^--J n/m_j. Prove total linear momentum conservation, normal relative velocity -e v_n and kinetic energy change -(1-e²)v_n²/[2(1/m_i+1/m_j)]. Tangential velocities are unchanged in this frictionless model. These are conditional mathematical collision laws, not a claim that restitution is constant in real materials. Event-driven integration invokes T10 transversality, dense trajectory/guard certificates, event separation, finite event count and restart residual error. Include collision search cost O(P²) naive and any spatial neighbor structure's actual assumptions. Simultaneous collisions, grazing v_n=0, dense frictional multi-contact and inelastic collapse/Zeno violate the isolated binary theorem; return explicit unresolved-event/budget status, or invoke a separately specified complementarity model. T11's scalar complementarity result is not advertised as uniqueness of arbitrary granular frictional contact. A DEM soft-contact penalty is a different ODE model; convergence of penalty to rigid impacts requires its own stiffness/restitution calibration limit and is not inferred from timestep convergence.
